_about: Hand-dated stories from the research passes. tools/newsdesk.py merges these into the brain's NEWSDESK block ahead of the RSS pull; each expires 21 days after `published`. Only headlines a paper printed — the brain may open with one, named as 'reported by <source>', and the law still comes from the shelf. Add rows at the top; never backdate.

items.source: DocOga research desk (BusinessDay 22 Jan 2026; Forvis Mazars Apr 2026; UNILAG circular Feb 2026)
items.title: Rent relief season is coming: from the 2026 tax year tenants deduct 20% of rent (max ₦500,000) — but only with a rent receipt in their name and a tenancy agreement; payroll desks start asking for evidence in December, employers file by 31 Jan, individuals by 31 Mar
items.note: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 s.30(2)(a)(vi). State exactly: 20% of annual rent paid, maximum ₦500,000, on accurate declaration with evidence. Never promise a naira amount saved; never call it automatic.

items.title: Viral video: Lagos landlord reportedly punched by tenant after proposing a ₦200k → ₦350k rent jump on a self-contain he had rented for six years
items.note: unverified footage, possibly staged — the brain may say 'a video circulating this week', never state it as fact

items.title: Residential rents under fresh upward pressure in Q4 2026 across Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt and Ibadan — housing group
States weigh tenancy reforms: agency fee capped at 10%, advance rent limited to one year, legal fee at 5%, rent tribunals proposed
items.note: proposals, not law — say 'proposed', never 'now the law'

items.title: Abuja poll: 71% say rent is much harder to pay than three years ago; 93% were asked for a full year upfront
Lagos mini-flat asking rents: Surulere ₦2.2m, Yaba/Gbagada ₦2.5m, Ikeja ₦3m, Lekki ₦4.8m a year
Lagos Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill — 5% agency fee cap and ₦1m fine for breaches — still a bill, not law, as of October 2026
items.note: the one correction readers need: the 2011 Law is still the law in force
